scope: Three proposed center-foam phases for enlarged island, pending native motion review. Approved sand source unchanged.

geometry.role: Geometry reference only; cropped view of actual approved ground export, no repaint

attempts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit / compositing.
Asset: one isolated transparent animation sprite, center shoreline foam phase006.
Image1 is a precisely registered geometry guide showing the APPROVED sandy shoreline. Image2 is the old phase006 foam for paint style and rhythm only; its curve no longer fits the new beach.
Create ONLY new thin white-cream foam strokes with little pale-cyan accents immediately BELOW the front edge of the sand in Image1. Follow its actual lower contour: a descending curve after the left inlet, a broad low middle, a small rise at the right inlet, then curving gently upward toward the right. We will lay this foam under/beside the unchanged sand. Do NOT include or redraw any sand.

Exact canvas1536x1024. Exact foam range x128..1407, y420..675. Foam begins near(132,440), sweeps down past(380,566) to(670,590), lifts gently past(990,540), then extends toward(1400,515). This guide is a close-up of the center coast, NOT the entire island ring. Leave everything outside that limited center shoreline segment transparent, especially x<128 and x>=1408. Maintain the fixed geometry; no zoom, centering, resizing, or moving the curve elsewhere.
At phase006 use two or three very slim, interrupted, flowing arcs and a few tiny adjacent flecks, with a 12-35pixel gap from the dark sand edge and no overlaps on the sand. Individual strokes about3-7px thick on this big canvas, delicately tapered, a little livelier at the left and center. Match Image2's hand-drawn cartoon white/cyan style but use Image1's contour and the positions above. Enough visible strokes throughout the width for a readable gentle lapping wave at quarter-size.
Genuine RGBA transparent background. No sand, dark outlines, shore illustration, solid blue water, cloud, glow, blur, shadow, people, objects, border or text. One single phase, no sprite sheet. The output is the isolated foam layer only.

references.role: historical foam style and phase rhythm
